THIS APPEAL

, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation in MVC No.1105/2018 dated 29.10.2021 passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Udupi.

sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties.
3.
The appellant was the petitioner-claimant before the Tribunal and the respondents were the owner, driver and insurance company respectively.
Therefore, the rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.
4. The case of the petitioner is that he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 02.09.2018.

It is NC:
2024:KHC:27814 alleged that on the date of accident at 12.30 pm, he was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-20-EP-8947 from Udupi to Saligrama side and when he reached NN-66, near Sugar Factory Dhoopadakatte, Baikadi, Udupi, a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-17-EV-8230 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the hind side of the motorcycle.
Thereby, the petitioner sustained injuries to the upper and lower limbs.
Hence, he filed the claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.1 being the owner and Respondent No.2 being the driver of the offending vehicle did not file any written statement.

Respondent No.3 insurance company appeared and filed written statement and contended that by denied the negligence of the offending vehicle is insured with an insurance company and accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. The Tribunal framed three issues.
The petitioner to prove his case, himself was examined as P.W.1 and a doctor was examined as P.W.2 and got marked thirteen documents as NC: 2024:KHC:27814 exhibits P.1 to P.13.
On behalf of the respondents, respondents did not lead any evidence and not marked any documents.

sentences.text: After hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.2,40,381/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization which is under challenge.
The Tribunal directed the respondent No.3-insurance company to satisfy the award amount and recover from the respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle, which is under challenge.
8. The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence on record.

The accident was occurred in the year 2018 and the notional income has to be taken at Rs.12,500/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.10,000/- per month and awarded the compensation towards loss of income for the laid up period, which is very less.
Hence, prayed for enhancement.
The learned counsel for the respondent has supported the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
It is further submitted to fix the liability on the owner of the vehicle (insured).

However,
the insurance company will pay the compensation and will recover the award from the insured.
10. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.

11. The point that arise for consideration is :
Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
12.
On perusal of records, it reveals that the petitioner sustained injuries to both legs.
He was admitted in the hospital for 15 days as inpatient.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering which in my opinion is less.
Therefore, I propose to award Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.

13. As regards special diet and nourishment, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,200/- and towards attendant charges it has NC: 2024:KHC:27814 awarded Rs.2,800/- and towards conveyance charges, it has granted Rs.4,000/-.

But considering the facts of the case and since the claimant was admitted to hospital for 15 days, I propose to award Rs.15,000/- towards food and nourishment,
conveyance charges and special diet.

14. As regards the loss of income during the laid up period, the petitioner is said to be running hotel business earning Rs.50,000/- per month, but due to injury, he was not able to do the business and he was taking treatment in the hospital.
Therefore, the grant of compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards the loss of income during the laid up period is very meager.
Since the accident is of the year 2018, I propose to consider the notional income as Rs.12,500/- per month and the laid period as two months.
is granted towards the loss of income during the laid up period.

sentences.text: As regards the loss of future income due to disability, this Court has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.12,500/- per months.

The doctor has opined that the claimant has suffered 13.39%
disability towards the whole body.

Therefore, NC: 2024:KHC:27814 taking the disability of 13.39%
towards whole body and the multiplier at 5, the loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.1,00,425/- (12500 x 12 x 5 x 13.39%).
16.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as follows:
Sl.
 Heads of compensation Amount in Rs.
No.
 1 Pain and suffering 60,000-00  2 Medical expenses 84,041-00  3 Loss of amenities 20,000-00  4 Loss of income during laid up period 25,000-00  5 Loss of future income on account of 1,00,425-00  disability  6 Food, nourishment, conveyance charges 15,000-00  and attendant charges
- 00  Rounded of to  Rs.3,04,500-00
As regards the liability there is no D.L. for the vehicle involved in the accident in question.
Therefore, the Tribunal ordered for directing the insurance company to satisfy the award and to recover the same from respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle.
There is no dispute and no appeal filed by neither NC: 2024:KHC:27814 owner nor the insurance company.
Therefore, finding of the Tribunal regarding liability is hereby confirmed.

17. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

awarded by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the respondent insurance company with interest at 6% per annum within a period of 60 days from the date of the receipt of copy of this judgment.
